title: Machine-learning probability scores for phaeochromocytoma and paraganglioma screening
summary: Models were trained on 2,046 patients and externally validated on 1,641; the five best reached AUCs of 0.988-0.994 and balanced accuracies of 0.958-0.981. Probability scores differed widely between models, and an artificial-neural-network model was selected as most robust. Ten specialists showed little improvement in interpretation after receiving the scores.
ai_technology: Machine-learning models (including an artificial neural network) on plasma metanephrines, methoxytyramine, age and pre-test risk
organization: University Hospital Carl Gustav Carus; Technische Universität Dresden

evidence.tested: Models were validated externally and their scores compared with predictions of ten clinical specialists before and after receiving them.
evidence.unknown: Whether scores improve clinical decisions is not shown. Abstract-based; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: ML models converted laboratory results into probability scores of disease.
